description: Composite figure of three scanning electron micrographs of Charpy V-notch fracture surfaces from as-solution treated and quenched Fe-Mn-Al cast steels. (a) is a high-magnification secondary-electron image (20 µm scale bar) of the 0.001% P specimen: a ductile tearing surface of equiaxed dimples and tear ridges, with small void nuclei or particles at the dimple bases, i.e. micro-void coalescence. (b) is a same-magnification image (20 µm scale bar) of the 0.07% P specimen: a low-energy cleavage-like surface dominated by long parallel striations, river-step lines and near-flat facets, with essentially no dimples. (c) is a lower-magnification image (100 µm scale bar) of the high-phosphorus specimen showing the larger-scale fracture morphology — large angular cleavage facets separated by ridges and secondary cracks that together form a dendritic, tree-like pattern. Read together, the panels demonstrate that raising phosphorus from 0.001% to 0.07% switches the fracture mode from ductile micro-void coalescence to brittle cleavage along {001} planes, which produces the dendritic pattern seen in (b) and (c). The caption attributes (a) to 0.001% P and (b) to 0.07% P; the citing text states notch toughness drops from 200 J to 28 J over the same change.
measured_quantities: notch toughness (J) — stated in citing text, not shown in the figure

observations.observation: Panel (a) shows a ductile dimpled-rupture surface with equiaxed dimples and tear ridges; dimple diameters are a few micrometres judging from the 20 µm scale bar.
Panel (b) shows a cleavage-like surface of long parallel striations and river-step lines on flat facets, with essentially no dimples.
Panel (c) is at a lower magnification than (a) and (b): its scale bar reads 100 µm whereas both (a) and (b) read 20 µm.
Panel (c) displays large angular facets bounded by ridges and secondary cracks arranged in a dendritic, tree-like pattern.
The caption states panel (a) is the as-solution treated and quenched 0.001% P Charpy V-notch specimen and panel (b) is the 0.07% P specimen.
The caption states the fracture mode transitions from ductile tearing in (a) to a low-energy cleavage-like fracture producing a dendritic pattern in (b and c).
The caption does not explicitly state which specimen panel (c) belongs to; it is only grouped with (b), so its attribution to 0.07% P is inferred rather than printed.
The citing text states solution-treated notch toughness decreases from 200 J to 28 J as phosphorus increases from 0.001% to 0.07%.
The citing text attributes the dendritic fracture pattern in the 0.07% P samples to fracture along {001} planes.
The citing text attributes the lowered cleavage strength of {001} to short-range ordering (SRO) of phosphorus, as predicted by Medvedeva et al.
The citing text gives the nominal steel composition as Fe-30Mn-9Al-1Si-0.9C with phosphorus varied between 0.001% and 0.07%.
No numeric value other than the scale bars (20 µm, 20 µm, 100 µm) is printed on any panel; there are no axis labels, curves or annotations in the figure.

subfigures.description: SEM fractograph of the as-solution treated and quenched 0.001% P Charpy V-notch specimen (20 µm scale bar): fully ductile dimpled rupture with equiaxed dimples, tear ridges and small void-nucleating particles; no flat cleavage facets visible.

SEM fractograph of the as-solution treated and quenched 0.07% P Charpy V-notch specimen (20 µm scale bar): low-energy cleavage-like surface with long parallel striations, river steps and flat facets; ductile dimples largely absent.

Lower-magnification SEM fractograph (100 µm scale bar) of the high-phosphorus fracture surface, showing large angular cleavage facets cut by ridges and secondary cracks that form the described dendritic pattern. The caption does not explicitly assign (c) to a specimen, but groups it with (b).

unreadable_items: caption is ambiguous about which specimen panel (c) depicts (no explicit label); attribution inferred from 'dendritic pattern in (b and c)'
